title: Strategic Pulse & Dependency Thermometer for Company OKRs
creator: Anna Patel
description:
Goal: Give leadership and cross-functional partners a lightweight, data-driven view ('Thermometer') of how company-level OKRs are progressing and where dependency heat (risk) is concentrated. This ticket scopes the first deliverable: a minimally opinionated dashboard + 4-week cadence playbook and escalation ladder that teams can adopt without heavy process overhead.

Why now: Roadmap complexity has increased with Dedicated and Private launches. We need a single, operational signal that surfaces: (1) OKR progress vs. planned milestones, (2) dependency chokepoints across orgs, (3) confidence and blocker signals from owners. Current status: limited manual rollups in spreadsheets and weekly slide decks that are slow to update and often stale.

What we'll build (MVP):
- Thermometer dashboard in the Console (or a shared LookerStudio) showing per-OKR progress bar, velocity trend (2- and 6-week windows), and dependency heatmap by team and priority.
- A 4-week Strategic Pulse ritual: biweekly asynchronous check-ins in Linear + monthly sync where the dashboard is the single source of truth.
- Lightweight dependency taxonomy and templated update message that owners post to Linear (OKR ID, milestone, blocking dependency, owner, ETA).
- Escalation ladder and SLAs for when a dependency is 'hot' (>2 weeks blocked or high cross-team operational cost).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
1) Dashboard wired to three canonical data sources: Linear issues tagged with OKR IDs, release milestones from GitHub projects, and a minimal manual override sheet for qualitative signals.
2) Dashboard refreshes within 6 hours of data changes and shows per-OKR progress % and a dependency risk score normalized 0-100.
3) Pilot with three cross-functional pods (Serving Runtime, Console, Dedicated) and a documented playbook with owners and meeting agenda.
4) Documented escalation steps and a named rotator for dependency triage during the pilot.

Design/trade-offs:
- We prefer a dashboard that consumes existing signals rather than forcing teams into new tooling. That keeps adoption friction low but increases complexity in the ingestion layer (mapping disparate fields).
- Chose 6-hour refresh window for MVP to limit infra work; real-time streaming can be a follow-up.
- Normalized risk score intentionally simple (heuristic combining time-blocked, number of teams dependent, and priority). This favors explainability over statistical sophistication.

Data & artifacts:
- Draft playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pm/strategic-pulse/thermometer-v1 (placeholder)
- Dashboard proto (LookerStudio): https://drive.google.com/example-thermometer-proto
- Linear template: /templates/okrs/dependency-update.md (to be added to org templates)

Stakeholders & reviewers:
- Executive sponsor: Maya Chen (COO)
- Engineering lead: Ravi Kumar (runtime)
- Design reviewer: Zoe Martinez (px)
- Data owner: Priya Singh (analytics)

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Teams won't tag Linear issues consistently. Mitigation: minimal required fields + a small 'data steward' assignment per pod for pilot.
- Risk: Dashboard becomes another status artifact ignored by teams. Mitigation: tie pulse to a monthly decision review; surface required actions (triage/no-op) rather than passive metrics.

Rollout plan:
Week 0-1: finalize taxonomy, get buy-in from pilot pods, mock dashboard review.
Week 2: wire Linear -> ingestion layer, implement risk-score heuristic, publish playbook.
Week 3-4: pilot run with biweekly asynchronous checks, collect feedback, iterate.
Week 5: decision gate — expand to full company or iterate on data quality.

Open questions:
- Should the risk score include scheduled capacity/hosts metrics from infra (cost-latency risk)? (owner: Ravi)
- Where does the authoritative OKR canonical text live? Confluence or a short-canonical field in Linear?
